title: waterfall-narrative-annotations-playtest-notes
body:
Overview:
This is a working playtest / sketch notes doc exploring a ‘narrative annotations’ layer on top of the waterfall/trace viewer. Goal: give engineers and incident responders a way to attach short, time-aligned narrative notes to spans (and groups of spans) that survive filtering and can be toggled on/off. Focused on interaction patterns, keyboard flow, and backlog-ready acceptance criteria.

Context / Why this exists:
- Current trace waterfall shows spans + timings but lacks contextual, human-authored signals (why a span is suspicious, temporary mitigation, link to runbook).
- We want a low-cost UX that supports quick annotations during incident triage and can later be curated into postmortems.
- Not intended to replace span metadata, traces should still be machine-first. Annotations are ephemeral until promoted.

Playtest setup (how we ran):
- 6 internal participants (SRE, infra PM, FE engineer, backend eng, support eng, product manager).
- Scenario: "spike in 95th percentile latency for customer X, root-cause unknown" simulated with synthetic trace patterns (long queue span, repeated DB retries).
- Tasks: mark first suspicious span, add a two-line annotation, create a grouped annotation covering retry span + backoff, filter to service-only view and verify annotation persistence, export annotations to linked incident.
- Duration: 45m session + 20m debrief.

Key interaction primitives sketched:
1) Inline span sticky note
   - Hover on span -> quick actions: flag (F), annotate (A), link-runbook (R).
   - Annotate opens a compact editor overlay anchored to span with small rich text (bold, code inline, link).
   - Editor autosaves to local draft every 3s; explicit save toggles promotion to shared annotation.

2) Group annotation / lane highlights
   - Lasso across timeline or shift+click select multiple spans -> create group annotation.
   - Group annotations show as a thin colored bar above the waterfall with summary text. Clicking expands the full note in side rail.

3) Narrative rail (side panel)
   - Rail shows chronological annotations for current trace with timestamps and author.
   - Each annotation lists: author, created_at, affected span IDs (clickable to jump), tags (manually entered), and status (draft | promoted | archived).
   - Promote: small CTA to push annotation to incident or postmortem (creates link in linked_artifacts).

4) Filter behavior and persistence
   - Annotations are independent of span filter state; when you filter to subset, a compact indicator shows that X annotations are hidden.
   - Toggling "show annotations" must not change current filter, but will re-anchor annotations to visible spans where possible (time-snap if span removed).

5) Time-scrubbing / timewarp interactions
   - Scrubbing playback keeps annotations pinned to their original timestamp; hovering timeline shows inline annotation tooltip.
   - If the span is collapsed (grouped) annotation stays visible in collapsed summary with an icon. Clicking icon expands group.

Accessibility notes:
- All annotation actions exposed via keyboard: focus span -> press A to open editor -> Esc cancels -> Ctrl+Enter saves and closes.
- Screen reader: annotations appear as a separate live region when promoted; ARIA labels include span name, annotation excerpt, author and timestamp.
- Color choices use patterned bars + text labels to avoid relying solely on hue.

Playtest observations / qualitative findings:
- Quick annotate on hover is used more than rail creation. People prefer in-context notes rather than switching panels mid-triage.
- Group annotations helpful for long retry chains; participants wanted an auto-suggest title when grouping (e.g., "DB retry storm 14:22").
- Concern: too many visible annotations clutter the waterfall; users requested clustering and prioritization heuristics (show only promoted or team-specific by default).
- Expectation mismatch: support engineers assumed annotations were immediately visible to the customer-facing team; need clearer "shared" vs "private/draft" state.

Edge cases we observed / considered:
- Span IDs are ephemeral between sampled traces — need to store time offsets and span path (service->operation->approx-start) so an annotation can be re-anchored across similar traces.
- When a span is trimmed due to sampling or partial trace shipping, show a ghost anchor in rail and mark as orphaned.
- Exporting annotations to external incidents should include context snapshot (screenshot / minimal span list) to avoid losing timeline context.

Proposed backlog items (rough JIRA style)
- JIRA-INT-4321: Implement inline annotate overlay (hover + A). Acceptance: open overlay, save, persistent in rail, keyboard flow implemented.
- JIRA-INT-4322: Group annotation by lasso/select. Acceptance: create group, colored bar appears, expand/collapse from rail.
- JIRA-INT-4323: Persist annotations across filters and add "hidden X annotations" hint. Acceptance: filtering does not delete notes, indicators present.
- JIRA-INT-4324: Annotation promotion flow -> incident export. Acceptance: clicking promote generates incident link and attached snapshot.
- JIRA-INT-4325: Accessibility pass (keyboard + screen reader ARIA regions).

Acceptance criteria (combined):
- An inline note can be created in <=5 seconds and saved with a single keyboard sequence.
- Notes are visible in side rail with accurate span jump targets 90% of the time for same-sampled traces in our test set.
- Hidden annotations indicator shows when filters remove annotated spans.
- Promotion attaches a minimal snapshot and returns a stable external link.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Storage model: store annotations in trace service vs. external notes DB (tradeoffs: replication, cross-trace search).
- Retention policy: default 30 days, team-configurable? Legal needs long-term retention for certain incidents.
- Permissions: who can create vs. who can promote? Should drafts be private-per-user?
- Clustering: algorithm for collapsing visually overlapping annotations (time proximity + author + severity).

Quick UI sketch notes (for designers/engineers):
- Compact overlay width 420px, max 6 lines preview in waterfall, full in rail.
- Small colored dot next to span name when annotated; color indicates state (draft amber, promoted green, archived grey).
- Keyboard hint text appears on first hover: "A = annotate • F = flag • R = runbook link" (dismissible).

Next steps / owners:
- Aisha: mock inline overlay + rail prototype (Figma) — due 2025-02-21.
- Miguel: spike on storage model and re-anchoring heuristics (2w).
- Priya: draft PRD section for privacy/permissions and retention (next sync).
- Samir: add exploratory e2e test scenarios to trace-sim harness.

Notes to self (loose):
- Consider adding tag auto-suggestions from span metadata (error codes, service name) when typing.
- If space, allow quick emoji/status marker (e.g., ⚠️ investigated, ✅ fixed) for rapid triage triage state.
- Keep annotations index lightweight to avoid adding overhead to trace ingestion pipeline.

End of doc — informal, iterate quickly.
